purpose: Rank authoritative free primary and scholarly sources before rule extraction; not verified books already read

regional_practice_layers.source_basis: Original Maya codices and securely interpreted glyph/date inscriptions
Modern Indigenous K'iche' participants and independent ethnography
Twentieth-century esoteric construction, independently date/provenance required

original_Maya_calendar_correlation_polic: GMT 584283 commonly used in historical reconstructions, but exact JDN convention and independently verified daykeeper continuity must be declared and tested; not selected in a chart engine by this registry.
first_task: Primary original Dresden page/facsimile and Smithsonian Indigenous education + Tedlock ethnography, then specialized Madrid and Bricker astronomy

source_records.title: Dresden Maya Codex
source_records.authors_or_holder: Maya scribal transmission; German SLUB manuscript facsimile
source_records.research_purpose: Original Postclassic calendar, rituals, eclipse/Venus and other astronomical tables; compare dated almanac passages to modern scholarly readings
source_records.interpretation_limit: Read digital original folio images with a separate keyed pagination/citation ledger; codex images not ingested by this register.

source_records.title: Living Maya Time: Calendar & contemporary daykeepers
source_records.authors_or_holder: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian / living Maya participants
source_records.research_purpose: Distinguish actual contemporary K’iche’ Chol Q’ij divination and living traditional calendar practice from modern pseudo-Mayan systems
source_records.interpretation_limit: Educational museum page and calendar converter; does not stand in for a formal ethnographic source or a tested individual birth-fate rule.

source_records.title: Time and the Highland Maya (revised ed., 1992)
source_records.authors_or_holder: Barbara Tedlock; University of New Mexico Press
source_records.research_purpose: Highest priority book for K’iche’ contemporary daykeeper interpretive methods, ethnographic social/ritual context and calendrical divination
source_records.interpretation_limit: Book not acquired/read in this track; contemporary K’iche’ is not identical to every ancient Classic Maya system.

source_records.title: Maya Calendar and Mesoamerican Astronomy
source_records.authors_or_holder: Gerardo Aldana; Encyclopedia of the History of Science
source_records.research_purpose: Decipherment cautions, origins of calendar astronomy, 260-day count, reinterpretations of supposed astronomical text
source_records.interpretation_limit: Use historical context and source criticism, not blanket validation of natal fate claims.

source_records.title: The Madrid Codex: New Approaches to Understanding an Ancient Maya Manuscript
source_records.authors_or_holder: Gabrielle Vail and Anthony F. Aveni (eds); University Press of Colorado, 2004 (updated paperback 2009)
source_records.research_purpose: Technical edition and interpretation of original Maya almanacs/ritual dates, Tzolk’in tables, context and links to broader Mesoamerican sources
source_records.interpretation_limit: Book not ingested. The edited interpretation is separate from the manuscript original; no individual personality rule assumed.

source_records.title: Astronomy in the Maya Codices
source_records.authors_or_holder: Harvey M. Bricker and Victoria R. Bricker; American Philosophical Society (2011)
source_records.research_purpose: Most important detailed academic codex astronomical and calendar-mechanics comparison, especially Venus, Mercury, eclipse/Mars and dates
source_records.interpretation_limit: Large specialist reference, not a pre-verified reading of every code page; astronomy precision does not equal natal behavioral predictive accuracy.

source_records.title: Skywatchers: A Revised and Updated Version of Skywatchers of Ancient Mexico
source_records.authors_or_holder: Anthony F. Aveni; University of Texas Press (2001)
source_records.research_purpose: Broader independent Mesoamerican archaeoastronomy and sky/calendar measurement context for selecting testable calculation claims
source_records.interpretation_limit: Regional synthesis rather than a codex itself or a single Maya natal divination rulebook.

source_records.title: Maya Calendar Origins: Monuments, Mythistory, and the Materialization of Time
source_records.authors_or_holder: Prudence M. Rice; University of Texas Press (2007)
source_records.research_purpose: History of the 260-day/365-day calendars and their political/cosmological origins
source_records.interpretation_limit: Rice's origin scenario is a research hypothesis, not an established earliest historical account or human astrology validation.

source_records.title: Other surviving original Maya codices (Madrid, Paris, Maya Codex of Mexico)
source_records.authors_or_holder: Institutional owner/catalog summary: SLUB Dresden cross-codex inventory
source_records.research_purpose: Separate original Maya Madrid almanacs, Paris K'atun calendar/zodiac, and Mexico Venus manuscript for comparison against Dresden
source_records.interpretation_limit: Catalog page, not an independent facsimile download. Read individual original manuscript reproductions before rule extraction.

source_records.title: The Maya Calendar System
source_records.authors_or_holder: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian (Living Maya Time)
source_records.research_purpose: Names 20 Tzolk’in/Chol Q’ij signs, 13 coefficients, 365-day Haab, regional K’iche’/Yucatec vocabulary
source_records.interpretation_limit: Educational handout rather than a primary source in which every day-name is a personality prognosis.

source_records.title: Popol Vuh: The Mayan Book of the Dawn of Life
source_records.authors_or_holder: Dennis Tedlock (trans., revised ed. 1996); Smithsonian bibliographic record
source_records.research_purpose: K’iche’ cosmology, historical/ritual symbolism and texts about cosmic order
source_records.interpretation_limit: Important context, NOT a direct natal horoscopy manual; don't infer birth-sign meanings.

source_records.title: Cycles of Time and Meaning in the Mexican Books of Fate
source_records.authors_or_holder: Elizabeth Hill Boone (2007); University of Texas Press
source_records.research_purpose: Explicit contrasting Mexica/Nahua and allied Mesoamerican divinatory codices and birth-fate almanacs; related 260-day count but distinct culture
source_records.interpretation_limit: Cross-Mesoamerican comparator, NOT an ancient Maya daykeeper source; keep tradition IDs independent.

source_records.title: Calendrical Calculations: The Ultimate Edition; Mayan calendar chapter and source algorithms
source_records.authors_or_holder: Edward M. Reingold and Nachum Dershowitz; Cambridge University Press (2018)
source_records.research_purpose: Established independent Gregorian/Julian/Long Count/Haab/Tzolk'in computational reference and code, as an alternative to building a new converter
source_records.interpretation_limit: Correlation, day epoch conventions and living K’iche’ daykeeping continuity still require source declarations; an accurate converter is not a personality predictor.

source_records.title: Maya Long Count conversion: configurable correlation constant
source_records.research_purpose: Independent reference lookup with explicitly configurable GMT 584283 versus other Long Count correlations; golden calculations for an eventual Maya calendar engine
source_records.interpretation_limit: Do not ingest dynamically displayed today's date as a timeless fixture; specific input/output pairs must be recorded and verified.

source_records.title: Maya/Mesoamerican original codices facsimile index
source_records.authors_or_holder: Foundation for the Advancement of Mesoamerican Studies (FAMSI)
source_records.research_purpose: Additional facsimile access and manuscript/codex lineage cross-comparison rather than reliance on one edited online codex text
source_records.interpretation_limit: Facsimile images and scholarly interpretive commentary are distinct evidence records; no raw original folio was read during this discovery.
